description: Validate p>=2, then deterministic is_prime(p), before reducing a. p=2 or residue zero returns a%p. Euler criterion rejects nonresidues. For p-1=q*2^s, find the first quadratic nonresidue z by ascending search, set c=z^q, x=a^((q+1)/2), t=a^q, m=s. While t!=1, choose least i with t^(2^i)=1; multiply x by c^(2^(m-i-1)), square that correction into c, update t and m=i. Return min(x,p-x). Tonelli-Shanks follows the method described by Shanks, Five Number-Theoretic Algorithms (1972).
state: For nonzero residue: x²=a*t mod p, c has order 2^m, t has order dividing 2^(m-1); each round reduces m, so i<m and shifts are below64. p prime guarantees nonresidue search termination before p. Residues and products fit u64 and u128 respectively.
cost: Primality O(log p), ascending search at most p-2 Euler exponentiations, and at most63 reducing rounds with O(log² p) total modular work. O(p log p + log² p) worst-case modular operations, O(1) space. No random expected-time or small worst-case search claim.
